title: Forest Rescuer
playerExperience: You walk through forest paths finding injured or lost pets. You carry each one to the sanctuary, heal them with found items, and reunite them with owners or keep them safe. You earn coins for successful rescues, unlock new forest areas, and watch your sanctuary grow. The loop repeats: explore, rescue, heal, return—no combat, no penalties while away.
visualDirection: A top-down or side-scrolling view of interconnected forest clearings. Each area shows injured pets in tall grass or by trees. You carry a pet visibly on your character as you walk to the sanctuary building. The shelter interior shows rescued pets resting in stalls, gradually recovering from distressed to calm animations.
assumptions: Progression motivation is emotional attachment: players return to see rescued pets recover and settle into the sanctuary, not to train or compete.
Each forest path unlocks after completing a set number of rescues (e.g., 5 rescues = new area), creating natural pacing.
Healing uses simple collected items (berries, water, bandages) found during exploration or earned as rescue rewards.
A rescue succeeds when you bring the pet to the sanctuary; no failure state or time pressure during the rescue itself.

firstPlaytest.goal: Verify that one complete rescue loop—find a pet, carry it to sanctuary, heal it, see it recover—takes 2–4 minutes and feels satisfying.
steps: Manually place one injured pet in a forest clearing 10–15 seconds' walk from the sanctuary.
Walk to the pet, press 'pick up' or approach to carry it.
Walk the pet to the sanctuary building.
Use one found healing item (e.g., click 'bandage') to begin recovery.
Observe the pet animate from distressed to calm over 10–20 seconds.
firstPlaytest.expected: The pet visibly changes state (limping → walking normally, sad face → calm), and you feel a sense of completion. No confusion about where to go or what to do next.
